events.title: Battle of Towton
events.description: In a blinding snowstorm in Yorkshire, the Yorkist army of Edward of York defeated the Lancastrian forces of Margaret of Anjou. It is often described as one of the largest and bloodiest battles ever fought on English soil.
events.significance: The victory led to Edward being crowned King Edward IV. It was a turning point in the Wars of the Roses.

events.title: Cumberland Road Authorized
events.description: President Thomas Jefferson approved the construction of the Cumberland Road. It was one of the first major improved highways in the United States and the first built with federal funds.
events.significance: The road, known as the National Road, linked the Atlantic seaboard to the interior. It helped open the American frontier to settlement and commerce.

events.title: Niagara Falls Runs Dry
events.description: An ice jam at the head of the Niagara River choked the flow of water. For about 30 hours, the thundering falls fell silent.
events.significance: Locals walked on the exposed riverbed. The event remains one of the most startling natural curiosities in North American history.

events.title: Mangal Pandey's Revolt at Barrackpore
events.description: Mangal Pandey, a sepoy in the 34th Bengal Native Infantry, attacked his British officers. His act came amid rising anger over the new rifle cartridges, which soldiers believed were greased with animal fat.
events.significance: His act is widely seen as a spark for the Indian Rebellion of 1857. It became a powerful symbol in India's story of resistance to colonial rule.

events.title: Mariner 10 Flies by Mercury
events.description: NASA's Mariner 10 probe passed close to Mercury. It was the first spacecraft to visit the innermost planet.
events.significance: The probe returned the first close-up images of Mercury's cratered surface. It also showed that Mercury has a magnetic field.
